title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered the issue 'No' and denied Complainant Michael A. McNeil's complaint, upholding the lower court's denial/approval of the judicial commission report rejecting his complaint against the Severna Park session's December 4, 2008 refusal to receive his charges against his wife. No separate relief was granted.
first_summary: The SJC affirmed Chesapeake Presbytery's denial of Michael McNeil's complaint against his session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife. The court deferred to the lower courts' factual and discretionary findings, found no clear error, and upheld the conclusion that the wife did not sin by going to civil court. The complaint was denied.
summary: The SJC denied a censured husband's complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery's approval of a judicial commission report, which had upheld his session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after she filed for civil divorce. Applying BCO 39-3.2–3.3, the SJC deferred to the lower courts' factual and discretionary findings absent clear error. It found no clear procedural error, upheld the conclusion that the wife did not sin by seeking civil protection, and invoked BCO 31-8's caution about accusations from one under censure.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: SJC Case 2009-22, adopted with 18 concurrences, 2 disqualifications, 4 absent; summary by RE Terry Jones, issue/judgment/reasoning by TE Bill Lyle with TE Greco and SJC amendments (lines 13, 80, 82–90).
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainant Michael McNeil challenged Chesapeake Presbytery's September 19, 2009 approval of its Judicial Commission report, which denied his complaint against the Severna Park Session's December 4, 2008 refusal to receive his charges against his wife (lines 17–36).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered the issue 'No' and denied the complaint (lines 40–45, 78). It applied BCO 39-3.2–3.3 deference to lower-court factual and discretionary findings absent clear error, and BCO 31-8 caution about accusations from one under censure; it found no clear procedural error and no error in the lower courts' conclusion that Mrs. McNeil did not sin in appealing to civil court (lines 47–78).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC reviewed the lower courts' findings; it did not conduct a new trial. The session had found McNeil guilty of abusive, selfish, and controlling behavior and imposed Admonition (lines 17, 31–33, 72). Mrs. McNeil's civil divorce filing preceded delivery of the session's November 18, 2008 judgment (lines 17–23).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The Chesapeake Presbytery Judicial Commission report denying the complaint, approved by CP on September 19, 2009, is not reproduced; its result is stated in the SJC report (line 36). No separate incorporated SJC opinion is supplied.
